correctness.rationale: For full-dimensional 3D zonotopes with parallel generating directions merged, the exposed-edge normal arrangement of each generator direction has exactly 2 k_i sectors, proving E=2 sum_i k_i. Every k_i >=2. The exhaustive rank-three configurations yield E=12 only with 3 independent directions (parallelotope), E=18 only with 3 distinct directions in a plane and one outside (affine prism over a genuine centrally symmetric hexagon), and E>=24 in every other case. For >=5 directions either four have no coplanar triple, or three span a plane and a fifth generator inside/outside that plane forces at least 12 total plane incidences. For any 3-polytope the number of complete vertex-edge-facet flags is F=4E. Hence Δ=(8/9)E−M. The symmetric 3D Blaschke–Santaló upper bound M<=16π²/9 implies the E>=24 lower bound (8E−16π²)/9. For an affine hexagonal prism H×[-1,1], integration of the polar support-function sections gives polar 3-volume (2/3)area(H°) and product M=(4/3) area(H)area(H°)<=4π²/3 by the planar symmetric Blaschke–Santaló inequality. Thus its Δ>=16−4π²/3 >0. For a parallelotope E=12 and exact centered product 32/3, so Δ=0. Polarity preserves Mahler product and reverses complete flags; Z° has zero deficit iff it is the polar cross-polytope of a parallelotope. The larger E>=24 bound exceeds the prism bound by (4/9)(12−π²)>0. No inference from finite examples to the universal theorem.

value.rationale: The object is the natural infinite class of all 3D zonotopes and duals of zonotopes, and the invariant Δ is the exact quantitative deficit in a recent published Mahler–flag inequality whose equality characterization was explicitly left conjectural. The result answers equality for the entire class and identifies a positive geometry-independent absolute margin once the extremal parallelotope/cross-polytope is excluded. The nontrivial 18-edge hexagonal-prism chamber forces a separate 2D product input, while the remaining E>=24 chamber enjoys a strictly larger margin. This is a mathematically motivated sharp qualitative boundary/equality classification, even though the explicit constant is nonoptimal and its known sublemmas are elementary. No paper-sized/general theorem or formal proof is demanded and no new general Mahler inequality is claimed.
